findingStatement: Saffire-I specimen geometry: large-scale SIBAL fabric panel measuring 40.6 cm wide by 94.0 cm long by 0.4 mm thick (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass blend).
applicableConditions: Thermally thin composite fabric (Bi << 0.1), uncrewed Cygnus flow tunnel
limitations: Directly applies to SIBAL fabric weave; does not represent structural thick thermoplastics.

findingStatement: Nominal Cygnus cargo vehicle cabin pressure during Saffire-I combustion was 101.3 kPa (14.7 psia, standard sea-level air).
applicableConditions: Cygnus OA-6 post-unberth free flight, nominal atmosphere (101.3 kPa, 21% O2)
limitations: Tested strictly in sea-level atmosphere; does not provide data for 56.5 kPa Exploration Atmospheres.

findingStatement: Forced concurrent airflow across SIBAL fabric was actively maintained at 20.0 cm/s (20-25 cm/s flow envelope).
applicableConditions: Fan-driven flow tunnel (0.5 m x 0.5 m cross section), concurrent flow vector
limitations: Single velocity setpoint (20 cm/s); does not capture low-velocity quenching boundary (<2 cm/s).

findingStatement: Saffire-I established steady-state concurrent flame spread of 2.0 to 2.5 mm/s (~2.4 mm/s) over large-scale SIBAL fabric without runaway acceleration.
applicableConditions: Concurrent forced airflow 20 cm/s, nominal cabin air (101.3 kPa, 21.5% O2)
limitations: Dynamic spread rates were derived from video pyrometry analysis, not recorded in the PSI specimen table.

findingStatement: Calculated vehicle cabin pressure rise from combustion thermal expansion is Delta P approx 3.8 kPa (bulk Delta T approx 11 K in sealed 18.9 m^3 volume).
applicableConditions: Cygnus pressurized module (sealed volume approx 18.9 m^3, 101.3 kPa)
limitations: Theoretical ideal-gas calculation, not a measured empirical transducer point in Urban et al. (2019).

findingStatement: Saffire-I demonstrated an absence of buoyant necking in microgravity, forming a broad, uniform, parabolic flame base spanning the fabric width.
applicableConditions: Microgravity (~10^-6 g), concurrent flow 20 cm/s
limitations: Qualitative optical morphology observation.

findingStatement: Concurrent flame spread over PMMA slab/card configuration propagated at ~0.18 mm/s, demonstrating that non-charring thermoplastic PMMA propagates an order of magnitude slower than thin cellulosic/fiberglass SIBAL fabric.
applicableConditions: Nominal cabin air (101.3 kPa, 21% O2, 20 cm/s flow), thick card configuration
limitations: Applies to thick polymer card configuration; direct scaling to thin PMMA films requires correcting for thermal Biot number.

findingStatement: A transient vehicle pressure rise of Delta P approx 0.5 kPa was cited in preliminary telemetry notes.
applicableConditions: Cygnus pressurized module
limitations: Unverified against peer-reviewed publications or raw OA-6 transducer logs; barred from being presented as confirmed measurement.

findingStatement: BASS-II forced flow velocity test envelope spanned 0.0 to 55.0 cm/s for PMMA rods and 1.0 to 25.0 cm/s for flat slabs in the ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox.
applicableConditions: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox flow duct, subsonic flow
limitations: 0 to 55 cm/s applies to axial stagnation rods; flat slabs tested over 1 to 25 cm/s.

findingStatement: In BASS-II, opposed-flow flame spread over cylindrical PMMA rods showed low-speed radiative quenching below approximately 1.0 to 1.5 cm/s, exhibiting a non-monotonic flammability boundary.
applicableConditions: Microgravity Science Glovebox, cylindrical PMMA rods (dia 6.35 - 12.7 mm)
limitations: Pertains to thick cylindrical PMMA rods in opposed stagnation flow; DOES NOT apply directly to thin PMMA films.

findingStatement: BASS-II demonstrated high-speed aerodynamic blowoff limits (15 to 50 cm/s depending on oxygen mole fraction), mapping a complete C-shaped flammability boundary for PMMA rods.
applicableConditions: Cylindrical PMMA rods, varying O2 concentrations (13.6% - 22.2%)
limitations: Applies to stagnation-point flows on solid rods; not applicable to concurrent thin fabric flames.

findingStatement: BASS-II Bhattacharjee test series mapped flame spread over thin PMMA films (100, 200, 300 micron) in a small flow duct with discrete fan display settings (47 to 62).
applicableConditions: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox nominal air, uncalibrated flow indices
limitations: Fan display setting is an integer dial (47-62); true flow velocity in cm/s is uncalibrated without duct calibration curves.

findingStatement: Isolated hydrocarbon droplets burning in quiescent microgravity obey quasi-steady d^2-law burning with hot-flame burning rate constant K approx 0.5 to 0.7 mm^2/s in standard air.
sourcePublication: Nayagam et al. (2015); Mikami et al.
applicableConditions: Quiescent microgravity (u_infty = 0), spherical droplet geometry
limitations: Hot-flame range is classical literature baseline; Nayagam (2015) focuses on cool-flame rates (0.2-0.3 mm^2/s).

findingStatement: FLEX proved that large isolated n-heptane droplets extinguish radiatively at finite diameters (d_ext > 0) in microgravity due to radiative heat loss, leaving unburned fuel.
applicableConditions: Quiescent microgravity, isolated n-alkane droplets (d0 = 1.5 - 5.0 mm)
limitations: FLEX records are deferred from active indexing; liquid droplet evaporation does not provide empirical evidence for solid pyrolysis.

findingStatement: Following hot radiative extinction, n-heptane droplets can transition into sustained low-temperature cool-flame combustion (T ~ 600-800 K) in the Negative Temperature Coefficient region without visible radiation.
applicableConditions: Low-temperature alkane chemical kinetics in microgravity
limitations: Liquid phase kinetics; cool-flame secondary deflagration on solid structural spacecraft materials remains an open research void.

findingStatement: Liquid droplet combustion data (FLEX) must not be cited as direct empirical support for solid material flammability due to fundamental differences between liquid evaporation and solid polymer pyrolysis.
applicableConditions: All microgravity regimes
limitations: Enforced as hard engine gate PHASE_INCOMPATIBLE.

findingStatement: Opposed-flow flame spread (conduction-limited) and concurrent flame spread (convective/radiant preheat) are physically distinct regimes that cannot be directly cross-scaled.
applicableConditions: All microgravity combustion
limitations: Enforced as hard engine gate FLOW_DIR_MISMATCH.

findingStatement: Thermal thickness scaling Vf proportional to 1/tau applies strictly to 2D opposed-flow conduction; concurrent flame spread does not follow a simple inverse-thickness relationship.
applicableConditions: Solid materials flammability scaling
limitations: Prohibits universal thickness extrapolations without geometry and flow regime qualification.

findingStatement: There is a complete empirical evidence gap for solid materials flammability in reduced partial gravity (Lunar 0.16g and Martian 0.38g). NASA PSI flight archives contain microgravity (10^-6 g) and ground 1g data, but partial-gravity transition boundaries remain untested in long-duration flight.
applicableConditions: Lunar and Martian surface gravity
limitations: Zero flight combustion data exists in current repository for partial gravity.

findingStatement: There is a major empirical evidence gap for materials flammability under Exploration Atmospheres (34% O2 at 56.5 kPa / 8.2 psia). Saffire-I and BASS-II tested strictly in nominal sea-level cabin air (21% O2 at 101.3 kPa).
applicableConditions: Artemis Exploration Atmosphere (34% O2, 56.5 kPa)
limitations: Existing Saffire-I and BASS-II flight data CANNOT predict flammability or extinction limits in 34% O2 exploration habitats.
